content.title: Variables: Give Values a Name
content.hook: A value is useful once. A named value can be reused.
content.context: JavaScript lets us give values names with `const` and `let`.
goals: Use variables to name values and understand assignment as storing a value for later use.

content.title: const
let
content.text:
Sometimes a name needs a new value later.

```js
let count = 1;
count = 2;
```

The first line gives `count` the value `1`. The second line assigns a new value, `2`, to the existing name.

Prefer `const` when the name does not need to be reassigned. Use `let` when reassignment is part of the job.

feedback.correct: The old value is `3`; `3 + 2` produces `5`, and that value is assigned back to `count`.
feedback.incorrect: The old value is `3`; `3 + 2` produces `5`, and that value is assigned back to `count`.

content.title: Build
content.text:
Write code that creates:

- a constant named `name` containing `"Maya"`
- a constant named `greeting` containing `"Hello, "` plus `name`

One valid answer:

```js
const name = "Maya";
const greeting = "Hello, " + name;
```

content.question: Which is the best reason to give a value a name?

options.text: It makes the value reusable and gives the code a readable label.
It automatically saves the value forever.
It changes a number into text.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: A. It makes the value reusable and gives the code a readable label.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: A. It makes the value reusable and gives the code a readable label.
